title: Reasons for Decline in Cancer Mortality despite Rising Diagnoses
what_it_is: Reasons for Decline in Cancer Mortality despite Rising Diagnoses

sections.label: Cancer mortality decline policies
sections.summary: The Ministry says lower cancer mortality has benefited all patients, with more work needed on prevention and early detection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health regarding the 21% decline in cancer mortality since 2012 despite rising diagnoses (a) what specific policy decisions or healthcare investments does the Ministry assess as most responsible for this improvement; and (b) how has the Ministry ensured these benefits reached lower-income and less health-literate Singaporeans equally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: They have lowered cancer mortality and have benefited all cancer patients, especially in systems like Singapore, where there is universal access to healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: That said, more work needs to be done especially in cancer prevention to modify risk factors such as smoking, unhealthy diet, lack of physical activity and alcohol consumption, encourage vaccinations that reduce the risk of specific cancers and detect the onset of cancer early through screening.

sections.label: Subsidy access gap and CDL
sections.summary: The Ministry does not publish thresholds, says its subsidy framework supports lower-income groups, and reports price reductions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And secondly, has the Ministry assessed whether the access gap between patients relying on subsidies and those who can pay privately, is widening and what would it cost to narrow the gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We do not publish the thresholds as this will have impact on our negotiating leverage with the industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On the second question, actually, our subsidy framework is already poised and framed to support those from the lower-income groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This is the whole point of the CDL because it is really nudging towards affordability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have already seen very good early results, we have seen a reduction in the price by about 30% on average and for some treatments, 60%.

sections.label: Availability of effective drugs
sections.summary: The Ministry says it can ensure the most clinically and cost effective drugs are available to all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We cannot stop that from happening; that is a fact of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But what we can do is to ensure that the most clinically effective, the most cost effective drugs are available to all.
